note: The county statements of the vote for the June 8, 2010 primary and the November 2, 2010 general election were searched for the text Mayor. Neither lists a Sacramento mayoral contest. Mayor elections in the city fall in 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024, so no mayoral election fell in 2010.

The county list of city officials gives the next mayoral election after 2024 as 03/07/2028, and the cycle is four years (2012, 2016, 2020, 2024). The county archive of elections for this year lists no Sacramento city election with a mayoral contest. No mayoral election fell in this year.

The mayoral nominating primary on 2012-06-05 elected the mayor by majority, so it is the decisive election. The county's qualified candidate list for the Nov 6, 2012 general election lists only City Council Districts 2 and 4 and a Charter Commission for the City of Sacramento; it lists no mayoral contest. The cycle comes from the County Elections Office voter information document for Measure A (Nov 2020), archived copy in additional_source_urls (original URL https://elections.saccounty.net/ElectionInformation/Documents/2020-Nov-General/FINAL%20-%20Measure%20A%20-%20City%20of%20Sacramento%20-%20Eng.pdf). Its charter text states that the mayoral office is elected in 2024 and every fourth year thereafter, and that the mayoral term is four years. This gives 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024 by four-year spacing. This is the proposed charter text of Measure A, so the cycle is stated for 2024 onward and 2012 to 2020 follow by the four-year spacing; the vote documents for each year show a mayoral contest. The county list of city officials was removed as a cycle source because it shows only the current mayor. The majority rule is stated in the City Clerk document cited in additional_source_urls (restated as proposed charter text, not the charter page).
